Microsoft Visual C++ runtime, deployed app-local
================================================

On a Windows install this file sits in the application directory next to
Manga Cleaner.exe, together with the Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime
libraries: MSVCP140.dll, MSVCP140_1.dll, VCRUNTIME140.dll, VCRUNTIME140_1.dll
and the rest of the CRT redistributable set.

Why they are here. The ONNX Runtime the application downloads on first launch
(runtimes/.../onnxruntime.dll) imports those four libraries in its ordinary,
non-delay-loaded import table. They are not part of the NuGet package that is
downloaded, and they are not part of a clean Windows installation: they arrive
with the "Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable", which a machine that has never
had a Visual Studio compiled application on it does not have. Without them
LoadLibrary fails with Windows error 126 and nothing in the application can
run, because every model session goes through that library.

Rather than ask the user to install the redistributable, or run Microsoft's
bootstrapper from an installer hook (which needs a network connection and
administrator rights the per-user install deliberately does not take), the
build copies the redistributable files into the application directory.
Microsoft's Visual Studio distributable code terms permit exactly this
"app-local" deployment, and the files are taken from the Redist tree of the
Visual Studio installation on the build machine.

Why the application directory and not somewhere tidier. onnxruntime.dll is
opened by `libloading::Library::new`, which calls LoadLibraryExW with no
LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_* flags, so its imports are resolved through the standard
search order. The first entry in that order is the directory the application
was loaded from, ahead of both the directory added by SetDllDirectoryW (which
crates/cleaner-core/src/runtime/mod.rs adds for DirectML and the WebGPU
plugin) and System32. A subdirectory beside the executable is not searched at
all, so these files have to be loose in the application directory.

What it costs. About 3 MB of installer, and the copies here do not receive
Windows Update servicing the way a machine-wide redistributable does. A CRT
security fix therefore reaches users through a new Manga Cleaner release
rather than through Windows Update.

Why this file exists at all. bundle.resources in tauri.conf.json is not
per-platform, and Tauri treats a glob that matches nothing as a build error.
The DLLs are staged into this directory by the Windows build only, so on a
macOS build this note is the only thing the glob matches, and it keeps that
build working. On macOS it ends up unused inside Manga Cleaner.app/Contents/
Resources.
